newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha softer, inter-month spreads unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha softer, inter-month spreads unchanged.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices slipped in late afternoon trade on Tuesday, mirroring weaker overnight crude markets, traders said.
Compared with crude slumps since early last week, however, losses in naphtha prices were relatively small, they added.
"Even though crude has dropped a lot since last week, naphtha has held up quite well," one trader said.

Bids for first-half January open-spec naphtha were heard at $212.00, while offers were assessed at $213.50. On Friday, it was quoted at $214.50/$216.50. The Tokyo products market was closed on Monday for a national holiday.
Second-half January was indicated about $1.00 below the first-half January level, traders said.
In inter-month naphtha spreads, second-half December/second-half January was quoted unchanged from Friday at plus $2.00/$3.00.

In middle distillates trading, importers have started probing the market for December cargoes, traders said. Japan is expected to import at least two to three spot cargoes for December, they said. Last year, Japan's kerosene imports in December jumped 46 percent from the month before.
